page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) via hyperthreading. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. This instance contains no local ephemeral storage and relies on network-attached volumes, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show average multi-core processing performance, indicated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 27992.16, a PassMark CPU score of 27240.11, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10181.0. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate middle-tier throughput, achieving 109.69 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 47.96 GB/sec for uncached writes. However, single-core execution capacity exhibits limitations, with weak stress-ng single-core results of 1312.39 and single-threaded gzip compression performance falling into the lower quartile. Application-level metrics reflect standard throughput, reaching 26.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.38 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6.8xlarge provides dedicated resource allocation for parallelized workloads without paying for high memory capacity or bundled local storage hardware. The lack of local NVMe storage necessitates external block storage configuration. The hardware profile and benchmark results fit this instance for compute-bound parallel workloads, software compilation, batch processing pipelines, web serving clusters, and intermediate database operations.
